correctness.rationale: For all positive a,b,D,r, the process is specified with no hit-triggered restart. Exit-side exponential transforms solve Df″=(r+s)f and renewal sums yield G_±(s); strong Markov continuation yields H_±(s). Differentiating the exact bivariate Laplace transform and independently computing the conditional first-exit moments gives E[T_-T_+] and the strict negative covariance. Rational elimination in x=e^A and y=e^B confirms the hyperbolic reduction identically; symbolic series checks the weak-reset cancellation, high-precision derivatives cover six nonsymmetric parameter sets, and three independent finite-lattice generator approximations converge. Positivity and denominators hold for all A,B>0. Lattice tests are not proof.

originality.rationale: Actual semantic scientific-record queries, exact formula/parameter searches, the accessible primary full texts of Linn–Lawley (2024), Pal–Prasad (2018), and Calvert–Evans (2021), and accessible own claim entries find known mean-cover or first-exit components but no exact continuing first-hit pair covariance or joint transform. The candidate computes a new second-order cross moment with a strict sign for every a,b,D,r>0 and establishes weak-reset cancellation; neither a published scalar mean nor a first-exit law implies that exact quantity without the additional stage calculation. Publication priority is best-knowledge and conditional on unindexed or unread related sources.
residual_risks: Full repository text of the related reflected cover-time-variance theorem was inaccessible; only the public scientific record summary could be compared.
An equivalent two-clock covariance could be implicit in unindexed specialist multi-target renewal literature; negative web/database search is not proof of novelty.
A 2025 paper with global-time correlations was checked by abstract only; its observable definitions differ, but complete manuscript noncoverage is not asserted.
The present theorem relies on familiar renewal and exit transforms, so specialists may regard its derivation as an accessible corollary even if its exact covariance is not explicitly published.

value.rationale: The joint reliability of a single searcher discovering both opposite targets is not measured by either one-target mean or the mean completion time. The exact negative covariance rigorously quantifies competing target searches for every target pair and rate, even under a shared reset clock. The cancellation of the leading weak-reset mixed moment is a structural, nontrivial asymptotic that governs fluctuations and is relevant to two-target completion distributions; no arbitrary parameter slice or trivial numerical increment is used. Limits include the absence of an extension to non-Poisson/different reset protocols.
